title: Ireland public data catalogue is already graph-scale
finding: The build connected 22397 catalogue datasets from 129 publishers into 22569 real-world nodes and 114818 candidate relationships.
caveat: Relationships are public-context links; many require source-specific adapters before exact spatial or temporal reasoning.

title: Weather and environment have broad public evidence
finding: The catalogue contains 2852 weather-tagged and 3461 environment-tagged datasets, giving flood and road-condition questions a broad evidence base before model training.
caveat: Catalogue metadata does not guarantee station-level or gridded observations are normalized yet.

title: Geospatial joins are possible but adapter-bound
finding: 4241 datasets expose geospatial formats or map-service signals that can support spatial joins across places, roads, services and hazards.
caveat: Candidate status is inferred from metadata; CRS, precision and geometry semantics still need validation per source.

title: Temporal context is widespread enough for change tracking
finding: 22395 datasets expose metadata timestamps or cadence signals, enough to drive freshness checks and versioned graph edge expiry.
caveat: Historical snapshots and event-time fields remain source-adapter dependent.

title: Most useful automation depends on machine-readable resources
finding: 21021 datasets currently have machine-readable resource signals, which is the practical substrate for automated ingestion and self-updating graph releases.
caveat: Machine-readable does not imply stable schema or permissible downstream reuse.

title: Flood context spans weather, rivers, terrain, land use and drainage
finding: The flood issue connects 6 distinct factor classes to public datasets, including rainfall, river levels, soil, terrain, land cover and drainage.
caveat: This is evidence coverage, not a flood-risk prediction.

title: Slippery-road forecasting needs both weather and road labels
finding: The graph now separates surface weather, road-network exposure and incident labels so slippery-road forecasting can be benchmarked instead of inferred from weather alone.
caveat: No accuracy is claimed until road-level event labels and temporal holdouts exist.

title: Harvest risk is not only a weather problem
finding: Bad-harvest context links growing-season weather, soil/land conditions and observed agricultural production labels, making crop forecasting a cross-domain evidence problem.
caveat: Crop-zone normalization and yield labels are required before predictive scoring.

title: Collision data is a smaller but high-value domain
finding: Only 73 datasets are tagged as collisions, but they anchor road-safety and slippery-road validation because they provide potential outcome labels.
caveat: Collision records need temporal and location granularity before event-level benchmarking.

title: Public-service access can be linked to transport and demographics
finding: Public-service (2408), transport (1590) and demographic (6041) datasets can be joined to explain service-access context.
caveat: Access analysis needs travel-time and service-status adapters before decision use.

title: Licence uncertainty is measurable
finding: 13 source records still require licence verification, so the graph can expose reuse risk instead of hiding it.
caveat: Reuse/export decisions must remain conservative until source-level terms are confirmed.
